edit.description: the bay-root refusal reports the top-level through the fold its own comparison computes, so the message's two roots are spelled alike

summary: The bay-root refusal prints git's top-level in git's alphabet beside a host-spelled bay root, so on win32 one message names two roots in two spellings

per.section: Bay discovery walks up to the nearest `.flume`

acceptance: the refusal names git's top-level in the one alphabet the rest of the message uses — the canonical form `bayRootDisagreement` already computes to make the comparison — so "naming both roots" is legible on every host and the paste target it offers is a host path
pins: flume refuses a bay root that is not the git top-level rather than composing paths against it
notes: Lane `windows`, run 36101405440: `tests/cli.test.ts:3361` reds — the message spells the top-level `C:/Users/...` and the bay `C:\Users\...`. `bayRootDisagreement` (`src/cli.ts:243`) folds `toplevel` at `:248` for the compare, then interpolates the raw value at `:251`, `:256`, `:257`. Fold once, report that; the lane's case needs no edit. No `tests[]` — posix spells both alike, so the lane proves the fix (the named exception in *A fix ships the test that would have caught it*).
